links.outcome: Rate of LLM acquiescence to inappropriate patient requests under multi-turn adversarial persuasion
links.effect: Acquiescence ranged 0% to 100% across 19 LLMs (bimodal); seven models held near-perfect guideline adherence, six acquiesced in most encounters; highest for CT requests, lowest for opioids.
links.quote: Across 19 contemporary LLMs and 1,425 simulated clinical encounters spanning three Choosing Wisely scenarios, acquiescence rates ranged from 0% to 100%, revealing a bimodal distribution.

links.outcome: Whether static medical benchmark performance, scale, or recency predicted robustness to patient pressure
links.effect: Model scale, recency, and static benchmark performance did not consistently predict robustness; static benchmarks judged insufficient to predict safety under sustained social pressure.
links.quote: Model scale, recency, and performance on static medical benchmarks did not consistently predict robustness.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-as-judge validated against physician raters (Cohen's kappa 0.957) to grade acquiescence in simulated encounters

screen.reason: Evaluates sycophancy and adherence to evidence-based guidelines across 19 LLMs using a multi-agent simulation framework under adversarial patient persuasion, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard/practice.
